It provides venous-thromboembolism context for surgical inpatients, supporting attention to postoperative ambulation and prophylactic management.

The postoperative-day-1 record shows a well-approximated dry wound, broadly stable vital signs, and about 100 mL of lightly bloody drainage; it records cefazolin prophylaxis after expander implantation and repeat CBC and related tests.

Consultation pathology states that the right-breast lesion is consistent with high-grade ductal carcinoma in situ with multifocal microinvasion; no malignant component was identified in the left-breast biopsy.

A second consultation pathology report more cautiously states that the right-breast lesion may be consistent with high-grade ductal carcinoma in situ with multifocal microinvasion, while no malignant component was identified in the left-breast biopsy.

Frozen sections of the right axillary sentinel and adjacent lymph nodes showed no definite malignancy, but paraffin sections were pending; frozen results must not be treated as the complete final pathology.
The report states that six right axillary sentinel and adjacent lymph nodes contained no carcinoma.
